title: 228. Portugal: The Golden Age of Discovery (Part 2)

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to the Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的余味》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: For bonus episodes, early access, ad-free listening, and access to our chat community, please sign up at restishistorypod.com.
sentences.zh: 想要获取加更集、抢先收听、无广告体验以及加入我们的聊天社区，请前往 restishistorypod.com 注册。

sentences.en: Tom Holland, I know you love a bit of Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德，我知道你很喜欢葡萄牙语。

sentences.en: I thought that was Dutch.
sentences.zh: 我以为那是荷兰语。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: That was absolutely pitch-perfect, fluent Portuguese, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是地道、流利的葡萄牙语，汤姆。

sentences.en: And I'm sure our Portuguese listeners will be writing in to offer their congratulations.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们的葡萄牙听众一定会写信来表达他们的祝贺。

sentences.en: Was that jugador de cricket?
sentences.zh: 那是“板球运动员”的意思吗？

sentences.en: I heard.
sentences.zh: 我听到了。

sentences.en: Nothing else to know, is there?
sentences.zh: 没什么别的需要了解的了，对吧？

sentences.en: It's actually worth doing this podcast purely for the pleasure of mangling continental languages, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 其实，光是为了享受那种胡乱拼凑欧陆语言的乐趣，做这档播客就值了，不是吗？

sentences.en: So yesterday, Tom, we kicked off our history of Portugal, this sort of epic story that we're telling.
sentences.zh: 所以昨天，汤姆，我们开启了葡萄牙历史的篇章，这是我们正在讲述的一段史诗般的故事。

sentences.en: And we got up to the death of Henry the Navigator.
sentences.zh: 我们讲到了航海家亨利的去世。

sentences.en: So the Portuguese, they've established this sort of medieval kingdom, one of many kingdoms on the Iberian Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人建立了一个中世纪王国，这是伊比利亚半岛上的众多王国之一。

sentences.en: They're not yet defining themselves against Spain.
sentences.zh: 他们当时还没有将自己与西班牙对立起来。

sentences.en: They have expanded to Madeira and the Azores, and they have this sort of sense of mission, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们已经扩张到了马德拉群岛和亚速尔群岛，并且有一种使命感，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Henry the Navigator died in 1460, and that's seven years after the Turks have captured Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 航海家亨利死于1460年，那是在土耳其人攻占君士坦丁堡七年之后。

sentences.en: Rome really has finally fallen, and Christendom is under attack.
sentences.zh: 罗马确实彻底陷落了，基督教世界正受到攻击。

sentences.en: And I don't know about you,
sentences.zh: 我不知道你怎么想，

sentences.en: but I think that's hugely important in explaining the kind of militancy and the sense of mission that the Portuguese have in the next sort of 50 to 100 years or so, don't you?
sentences.zh: 但我认为这对于解释葡萄牙人在接下来的50到100年左右所表现出的那种好战性和使命感非常重要，你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Though it obviously helps that it also makes them very rich.
sentences.zh: 尽管这显然也有助于让他们变得非常富有。

sentences.en: You're so cynical.
sentences.zh: 你真是太愤世嫉俗了。

sentences.en: Well, no, I mean, we talked about that in the last episode, the way that the lust for spice fuses with the sense that this is what God wants.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，我们在上一集讨论过，对香料的渴望与“这是上帝的旨意”这种信念是如何融合在一起的。

sentences.en: So Henry the Navigator, obviously, he is fascinated and obsessed by exploration, but he is also the grandmaster of the military order of Christ,
sentences.zh: 所以航海家亨利，显然，他痴迷于探索，但他同时也是基督军事修会的总团长，

sentences.en: which is a successor to the Knights Templar, the kind of the militant order of knights who fought in the Crusades.
sentences.zh: 这是圣殿骑士团的继承者，也就是在十字军东征中作战的那个好战的骑士组织。

sentences.en: So I think you get both, and I think that that kind of combination of greed and kind of Christian militancy, conviction that God wants you to go out and grab things from Muslims,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为两者兼而有之，而且我认为这种贪婪与基督教好战性的结合，即坚信上帝希望你去从穆斯林手中夺取东西，

sentences.en: explains why today's story, which is the story of Portugal's expansion down the coast of Africa and then into the Indian Ocean, is a bloody as well as a heroic story.
sentences.zh: 解释了为什么今天的故事——关于葡萄牙沿着非洲海岸扩张并进入印度洋的故事——既是一个血腥的故事，也是一个英雄的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是啊，这很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because when you read this story, and I should sort of shout out, there's a book by Roger Crowley called Conquerors that I reviewed a few years ago for the Sunday Times,
sentences.zh: 因为当你读到这个故事时——我应该提一下，罗杰·克劳利写过一本叫《征服者》的书，我几年前为《星期日泰晤士报》写过书评，

sentences.en: gave it a rave review, actually, because I really enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 实际上我给了它极高的评价，因为我真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: And he told it as an absolutely sort of rip-roaring, rollicking adventure story, although one completely soaked with blood.
sentences.zh: 他把它写成了一个绝对惊心动魄、跌宕起伏的冒险故事，尽管其中完全浸透了鲜血。

sentences.en: And it is one of these things where you sort of think there's so much fuss made about Columbus and about the conquistadors, but the Portuguese have sort of escaped all that.
sentences.zh: 这就像是那种你会觉得人们对哥伦布和征服者大惊小怪，但葡萄牙人却避开了所有这些关注。

sentences.en: Because nobody really, you know, people don't speak Portuguese in Anglo-Saxon countries, and they don't know what's happening.
sentences.zh: 因为没人真的，你知道，盎格鲁-撒克逊国家的人不说葡萄牙语，他们不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: But there's an awful lot of terrible violence, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但那里发生了大量可怕的暴力事件，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Columbus venturing out into the vast emptiness of the Atlantic, I mean, there's an inherent drama there.
sentences.zh: 所以哥伦布冒险进入大西洋的广袤虚无中，我的意思是，这本身就有一种内在的戏剧性。

sentences.en: But I think there is also an incredible drama in the idea of sailing down a landmass that you know nothing about.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，沿着一片你一无所知的陆地航行，这种想法也具有令人难以置信的戏剧性。

sentences.en: You don't know what you're going to find there.
sentences.zh: 你不知道在那里会发现什么。

sentences.en: And the way in which when these expeditions start going down Africa to try and get to India, they take with them these pillars, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而且当这些探险队开始沿着非洲航行试图到达印度时，他们随身带着这些柱子，不是吗？

sentences.en: Stone pillars.
sentences.zh: 石柱。

sentences.en: Stone pillars, and they set them up in bays as kind of way markers.
sentences.zh: 石柱，他们把它们竖在海湾里作为某种路标。

sentences.en: And I suppose you could say, well, you know, these are markers of colonization.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说，好吧，你知道，这些是殖民的标志。

sentences.en: I mean, it's almost a kind of an expression of impotence before the vastness of the task.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这几乎是一种在艰巨任务面前感到无能为力的表达。

sentences.en: And so all you can do is put one small stone pillar, the only mark that you can leave on the vastness of this, you know, strange lands full of strange creatures, strange peoples,
sentences.zh: 所以你唯一能做的就是立起一根小小的石柱，这是你能在广袤的、充满奇怪生物、奇怪民族、

sentences.en: strange plants.
sentences.zh: 奇怪植物的陌生土地上留下的唯一印记。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a very kind of – and I think also that when thinking about this, because we know what's going to happen, because we know the brutal history that's going to follow,
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种非常——而且我认为当思考这个问题时，因为我们知道将会发生什么，因为我们知道随后将要发生的残酷历史，

sentences.en: and we know that the Portuguese make it, and we know that in the long run, Europe is going to expand its hegemony across the world.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道葡萄牙人成功了，我们知道从长远来看，欧洲将把它的霸权扩张到全世界。

sentences.en: We need to park that and think that Portugal is a tiny peripheral power.
sentences.zh: 我们需要暂时放下这些，去想一想葡萄牙当时只是一个微小的边缘势力。

sentences.en: And the sheer kind of boldness and daring of what they're attempting, you know, you have to keep that in mind if you can have a sense of just how extraordinary a story this is.
sentences.zh: 他们所尝试的事情那种纯粹的胆识和勇气，你知道，如果你想感受一下这个故事是多么非凡，就必须记住这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这绝对正确。

sentences.en: So Henry the Navigator died in 1460, and the guy who takes over the sort of mission ultimately is his great-nephew, who is João, Prince João,
sentences.zh: 航海家亨利死于1460年，最终接手这一使命的人是他的侄孙，也就是若昂，若昂王子，

sentences.en: who becomes the king of Portugal in 1481.
sentences.zh: 他在1481年成为了葡萄牙国王。

sentences.en: And he's a sort of very melancholy, sort of lugubrious fellow.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常忧郁、阴沉的家伙。

sentences.en: He's got a long face, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他长着一张长脸，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's got a very long face and a black beard.
sentences.zh: 他长着一张非常长的脸和黑色的胡子。

sentences.en: The Portuguese remember him apparently as the perfect prince, and I read that Isabella, Queen of Castile, called him simply the man.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人显然记得他是完美的王子，我读到卡斯蒂利亚女王伊莎贝拉干脆称他为“那个人”。

sentences.en: Presumably she called him el hombre, because he was such an impressive fellow.
sentences.zh: 大概她称他为“el hombre”，因为他是一个如此令人印象深刻的家伙。

sentences.en: So he basically has this desire, like Henry the Navigator, to be rich, but he also is very into the Presto-John thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上有这种渴望，像航海家亨利一样，想要富有，但他也非常热衷于“祭司王约翰”的传说。

sentences.en: So the idea that there's a Christian kingdom out there that they can make an alliance with against the Islamic powers,
sentences.zh: 也就是认为外面有一个基督教王国，他们可以与之结盟来对抗伊斯兰势力，

sentences.en: and also, crucially, to find a route to the Indies, so to get the spices.
sentences.zh: 而且至关重要的是，找到通往印度的路线，从而获得香料。

sentences.en: And what's funny is he turns down Columbus.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他拒绝了哥伦布。

sentences.en: Columbus, I mean, actually, the funny thing is people always tell that story, and they say, the Portuguese want Muppets, they turn down Columbus.
sentences.zh: 哥伦布，我的意思是，事实上，有趣的是人们总是讲那个故事，他们说，葡萄牙人是傻瓜，他们拒绝了哥伦布。

sentences.en: Of course, they were quite right.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们完全是对的。

sentences.en: Columbus says, I can go west and find the Indies.
sentences.zh: 哥伦布说，我可以向西走找到印度。

sentences.en: And they say, yeah, don't bother me.
sentences.zh: 他们说，是的，别烦我。

sentences.en: Yeah, good luck.
sentences.zh: 是的，祝你好运。

sentences.en: We're going to go our way, and they do get that.
sentences.zh: 我们要走我们的路，他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: I mean, they weren't wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们并没有错。

sentences.en: Well, when in due course Vasco Tagovic does get to India, Manuel, who succeeds Jao, he writes to Ferdinand and Isabella and says,
sentences.zh: 好吧，当瓦斯科·达·伽马最终到达印度时，继任若昂的曼努埃尔写信给斐迪南和伊莎贝拉说，

sentences.en: he describes all the stuff that they found in India.
sentences.zh: 他描述了他们在印度发现的所有东西。

sentences.en: So all the cinnamon, the cloves, the ginger, the nutmegs, the pepper, the diamonds, the rubies, everything.
sentences.zh: 所有的肉桂、丁香、姜、肉豆蔻、胡椒、钻石、红宝石，应有尽有。

sentences.en: And he says, we are aware that your highness will hear of these things with much pleasure and satisfaction, which I think is splendid behavior.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们知道殿下听到这些消息会感到非常高兴和满足，我认为这是一种非常得体的行为。

sentences.en: That's like the way you behave to rival history podcasters, Tom, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就像你对待竞争对手历史播客的方式，汤姆，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Well, we all share.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们都分享。

sentences.en: We all take pleasure in each other's successes.
sentences.zh: 我们都为彼此的成功感到高兴。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然会。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然会。

sentences.en: So the first guy they send is this guy, Diogo Kao, and he goes down to – I mean, he goes a hell of a long way, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 所以他们派出的第一个人是这个叫迪奥戈·康的人，他去了——我的意思是，他走了非常非常远，我必须得说。

sentences.en: He goes to the Congo.
sentences.zh: 他去了刚果。

sentences.en: He sails a bit up the Congo, and he actually leaves a pillar there that's not discovered for another few hundred years.
sentences.zh: 他沿着刚果河航行了一段，实际上在那里留下了一根柱子，几百年后才被发现。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's dropping off these pillars everywhere.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他到处都在留下这些柱子。

sentences.en: Angola, Namibia.
sentences.zh: 安哥拉，纳米比亚。

sentences.en: I mean, Namibia, that's a colossal journey.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纳米比亚，那是一段巨大的旅程。

sentences.en: You know, it's such a long way, and we know so little about him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，路途太遥远了，而我们对他知之甚少。

sentences.en: And so, you know, actually, that's the case with some of his successes as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，实际上，他的一些继任者也是如此。

sentences.en: So they're sort of – they sail for 500 miles up the Senegal River.
sentences.zh: 所以他们——他们沿着塞内加尔河航行了500英里。

sentences.en: They go up the Gambia.
sentences.zh: 他们沿着冈比亚河向上游航行。

sentences.en: They're crossing the desert.
sentences.zh: 他们正在穿越沙漠。

sentences.en: They're going to Timbuktu.
sentences.zh: 他们正前往廷巴克图。

sentences.en: So the Portuguese are convinced that they can find the route to India, and also that they can find this guy, Presta John.
sentences.zh: 所以葡萄牙人确信他们可以找到通往印度的路线，而且他们也可以找到这个叫祭司王约翰的人。

sentences.en: And also gold, the supply of gold.
sentences.zh: 还有黄金，黄金的供应。

sentences.en: Yeah, because they know there's gold out there somewhere.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他们知道外面某个地方有黄金。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a bit like the Spanish in the Americas.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像美洲的西班牙人。

sentences.en: We all know the story of the Spanish in the Americas.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道美洲西班牙人的故事。

sentences.en: I actually like the Portuguese story better because it's so – it's not so hackneyed, is it?
sentences.zh: 我其实更喜欢葡萄牙人的故事，因为它太——它没那么陈腐，不是吗？

sentences.en: We don't know so much about it, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想我们对它了解得没那么多。

sentences.en: So the last pillar that Cowell sets up is on black rocks where seals are basking, and then he turns back round.
sentences.zh: 所以康立下的最后一根柱子是在海豹晒太阳的黑色岩石上，然后他就掉头回去了。

sentences.en: It's such a kind of powerful image.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有力量的画面。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the next guy is Bartholomew Diaz.
sentences.zh: 所以下一个人是巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士。

sentences.en: Bartholomew Diaz, I think, would be –
sentences.zh: 巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士，我想应该是——

sentences.en: That's how the Dutch would pronounce it.
sentences.zh: 那是荷兰人的发音方式。

sentences.en: Bartholomew Diaz.
sentences.zh: 巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士。

sentences.en: And that is how they say it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 而那正是他们说它的方式，汤姆。

sentences.en: That is how they say it.
sentences.zh: 那正是他们说它的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I was once on a train with – it's a very strange story, this.
sentences.zh: 我曾经和一个人在火车上——这是一个非常奇怪的故事。

sentences.en: I was going to Barcelona, and I was sitting in the compartment opposite a couple.
sentences.zh: 我当时正要去巴塞罗那，我坐在车厢里，对面是一对夫妇。

sentences.en: The man had no legs, and the woman had no arMs.
sentences.zh: 那个男人没有腿，那个女人没有手臂。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: I mean, it was very – they were a good team.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常——他们是一个很好的团队。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A very good team.
sentences.zh: 一个非常好的团队。

sentences.en: And they were Portuguese, and it was the first time I'd ever heard Portuguese people.
sentences.zh: 他们是葡萄牙人，那是我第一次听到葡萄牙人说话。

sentences.en: And they had this sort of – at first, I thought they were speaking Russian because there were so many of the sort of shh and the sort of yow kind of sounds.
sentences.zh: 他们有这种——起初，我以为他们在说俄语，因为有很多那种“嘶”和“哟”之类的声音。

sentences.en: And then I discovered they were talking Portuguese, and they said they could understand Spanish, but the Spanish couldn't understand them.
sentences.zh: 后来我发现他们在说葡萄牙语，他们说他们能听懂西班牙语，但西班牙人听不懂他们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so that's my great linguistic insight for today's episode.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是我今天这一集伟大的语言学见解。

sentences.en: Amazing, amazing podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 了不起，了不起的播客。

sentences.en: Thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Anyway, can we get back to Bartholomew Diaz?
sentences.zh: 总之，我们能回到巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士身上吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So he leaves – he's a knight.
sentences.zh: 所以他出发了——他是一名骑士。

sentences.en: He's one of Zhao's knights.
sentences.zh: 他是若昂的骑士之一。

sentences.en: And basically, Zhao says to him, off you go.
sentences.zh: 基本上，若昂对他说，你出发吧。

sentences.en: I'll give you two of these caravels.
sentences.zh: 我给你两艘这种轻快帆船。

sentences.en: Now, if you don't know what a caravel is, Tom gives a brilliant, brilliant excursion into naval technology.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你不知道什么是轻快帆船，汤姆在海军技术方面做过精彩绝伦的讲解。

sentences.en: Yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我做过。

sentences.en: In our previous podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 在我们之前的播客里。

sentences.en: Shallow bottoMs.
sentences.zh: 浅吃水。

sentences.en: And crucially, Tom, what else have they got?
sentences.zh: 而且至关重要的是，汤姆，他们还有什么？

sentences.en: They've got triangular sails.
sentences.zh: 他们有三角帆。

sentences.en: Triangular sails.
sentences.zh: 三角帆。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Triangular sails.
sentences.zh: 三角帆。

sentences.en: And what does that mean, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那意味着什么，汤姆？

sentences.en: It means that they can do what they like with the wind.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们可以随心所欲地利用风。

sentences.en: They can literally do what they like.
sentences.zh: 他们真的可以随心所欲。

sentences.en: Is that what it means?
sentences.zh: 是那个意思吗？

sentences.en: That's exactly what it means.
sentences.zh: 正是那个意思。

sentences.en: I think that's – I learned that from NAM Roger, the great naval historian.
sentences.zh: 我想那是——我是从伟大的海军历史学家罗杰那里学到的。

sentences.en: He told me – they were his precise words.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我的——那是他的原话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So they set off.
sentences.zh: 所以他们出发了。

sentences.en: They set off in the summer of 1487.
sentences.zh: 他们在1487年的夏天出发。

sentences.en: We know very little about Bartholomew Diaz.
sentences.zh: 我们对巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士知之甚少。

sentences.en: We don't even know when his expedition left, even though it's going to change the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不知道他的探险队是什么时候出发的，尽管它将改变世界历史。

sentences.en: Of the world.
sentences.zh: 世界的。

sentences.en: And he takes his stone pillars, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他带着他的石柱，对吧？

sentences.en: He takes his stone pillars.
sentences.zh: 他带着他的石柱。

sentences.en: They love a stone pillar in Portugal.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人很喜欢石柱。

sentences.en: Can't get enough of them.
sentences.zh: 怎么都看不够。

sentences.en: When they take them now, when they go on holiday.
sentences.zh: 他们现在带上石柱，去度假的时候。

sentences.en: Anyway, off they go.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们出发了。

sentences.en: They go for months.
sentences.zh: 一去就是好几个月。

sentences.en: And by Christmas, they're in about Namibia or so.
sentences.zh: 到了圣诞节，他们差不多到了纳米比亚一带。

sentences.en: They've been going for four months.
sentences.zh: 他们已经航行了四个月了。

sentences.en: And then they take this absolutely – so basically, the wind is against them, so they can't go any – they think they can't go any further south.
sentences.zh: 然后他们采取了——基本上，因为风向对他们不利，他们觉得不能再往南走了。

sentences.en: And then they take – this is where our grasp of naval technology will come in.
sentences.zh: 于是他们采取——这就是我们对海军技术理解派上用场的地方了。

sentences.en: Very useful time to explain this.
sentences.zh: 解释这个非常有用。

sentences.en: They take this radical decision.
sentences.zh: 他们做出了一个激进的决定。

sentences.en: So basically, instead of continuing to go south, they say, let's sail right out into the sea, to the west, into the nothingness.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们没有继续向南，而是决定直接驶向大海，向西，驶向虚无。

sentences.en: Because there, basically, the wind may kind of whip us around and take us in a big loop.
sentences.zh: 因为在那里，风可能会把我们卷起来，带我们绕一个大圈。

sentences.en: Well, because that's what happens north of the equator, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为赤道以北就是这种情况，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But the trade winds, you sail out – you go down Africa, you sail out west into the Atlantic, and then the trade winds blow you back to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 但信风会让你驶出——你沿着非洲海岸南下，向西驶入大西洋，然后信风会把你吹回葡萄牙。

sentences.en: I knew you were on top of all this, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我就知道你对这些了如指掌，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I knew you were on top of all this.
sentences.zh: 我就知道你对这些了如指掌。

sentences.en: The rest is navigation.
sentences.zh: 剩下的就是导航了。

sentences.en: That's what we will be called.
sentences.zh: 我们以后就叫这个名字。

sentences.en: I'm like, what's his name?
sentences.zh: 我在想，他叫什么名字来着？

sentences.en: Patrick O'Brien.
sentences.zh: 帕特里克·奥布莱恩。

sentences.en: It turned out, actually, that Patrick O'Brien – you know, the irony is it turned out that he was making it all up.
sentences.zh: 事实上，帕特里克·奥布莱恩——你知道，讽刺的是，后来发现他全是编的。

sentences.en: He didn't know anything about rope or ships.
sentences.zh: 他根本不懂绳索或船只。

sentences.en: Well, there you go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，原来如此。

sentences.en: No one would ever say that about this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 没人会这样评价我们的播客。

sentences.en: No, we know our navigation.
sentences.zh: 不，我们很懂导航。

sentences.en: So anyway, they take this massive loop out into the Atlantic, Bartholomew Diaz and his guys.
sentences.zh: 总之，巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士和他的船员们在大西洋上绕了一个大圈。

sentences.en: And then they turn around and they see these mountains.
sentences.zh: 然后他们转过身，看到了这些山脉。

sentences.en: And basically what's happened is they have been carried by the winds in this great loop around the Cape of Good Hope.
sentences.zh: 基本上发生的事情是，他们被风带到了好望角周围的一个大环线上。

sentences.en: And they have gone around the bottom of Africa.
sentences.zh: 他们绕过了非洲的最南端。

sentences.en: And they make landfall eventually on what's now the Eastern Cape.
sentences.zh: 最终在现在的东开普省登陆。

sentences.en: In Mussel Bay.
sentences.zh: 在穆塞尔湾。

sentences.en: Is that what it's called?
sentences.zh: 是叫这个名字吗？

sentences.en: Mussel.
sentences.zh: 穆塞尔（Mussel，贻贝）。

sentences.en: So it's Dutch for muscle.
sentences.zh: 所以这是荷兰语里的“贻贝”。

sentences.en: Oh, that's lovely.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太可爱了。

sentences.en: So you've got a bit of Portuguese, a bit of Dutch in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个播客里，你既能听到一点葡萄牙语，也能听到一点荷兰语。

sentences.en: Not only do you get top naval technology, you get great European languages.
sentences.zh: 你不仅能学到顶尖的海军技术，还能学到很棒的欧洲语言。

sentences.en: It's like a university in itself.
sentences.zh: 这本身就像一所大学。

sentences.en: We're offering all kinds of modules.
sentences.zh: 我们提供各种各样的课程模块。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So anyway, they pitch up.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们靠岸了。

sentences.en: The natives, they are not very keen, are they?
sentences.zh: 当地人不太欢迎他们，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实。

sentences.en: And they're right not to be keen, basically, because these kind of peculiar people with white skins and guns and a tendency to enslave you.
sentences.zh: 他们不欢迎是对的，因为这些皮肤白皙、带着枪支且有奴役倾向的怪人出现了。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you don't want to hang around when they turn up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得当他们出现时，你肯定不想待在附近。

sentences.en: Well, there's this sort of story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有这样一个故事。

sentences.en: When Diaz was taking in water close to the beach, they sought to prevent him.
sentences.zh: 当迪亚士在靠近海滩的地方取水时，当地人试图阻止他。

sentences.en: And when they pelted him with stones from a hill, he killed one of them with the arrow of a crossbow.
sentences.zh: 当他们从山上向他投掷石块时，他用弩箭射杀了一个人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that, I suppose, is the sort of test the template, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想，这算是定下了基调，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's going to be an awful lot of killing people with crossbows and things in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 因为在这个播客里，会有很多用弩箭杀人的事情发生。

sentences.en: So then the Portuguese turn around and Bartholomew Diaz, they sail all the way back.
sentences.zh: 于是葡萄牙人掉头，巴托洛梅乌·迪亚士他们一路航行回去。

sentences.en: When they go around the Cape, apparently they first called it the Stormy Cape because it was very stormy and King Zhao doesn't like that at all when they get back.
sentences.zh: 当他们绕过海角时，据说他们最初称其为“风暴角”，因为那里风暴很大，若昂国王回来后一点也不喜欢这个名字。

sentences.en: And he says, you can't call it that because it's sort of too downbeat.
sentences.zh: 他说，你不能叫它那个名字，因为它太消极了。

sentences.en: So they turn it to the Cape of Good Hope because it promises, holds out hope that one day they'll get to India.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把它改名为“好望角”，因为它预示着、带来了有一天能到达印度的希望。

sentences.en: And when they've gone around the Cape of Good Hope, they've left behind their supply ship, which isn't a caravel.
sentences.zh: 当他们绕过好望角时，他们丢下了补给船，那不是一艘卡拉维尔帆船。

sentences.en: So it doesn't have a flat bottom, Dominic, or a triangular sail.
sentences.zh: 所以它没有平底，多米尼克，也没有三角帆。

sentences.en: So it can't do what they've just done.
sentences.zh: 所以它做不到他们刚才做到的事。

sentences.en: Useless.
sentences.zh: 没用。

sentences.en: Absolutely useless.
sentences.zh: 完全没用。

sentences.en: And they find that it's absolutely, it's been eaten up by worMs.
sentences.zh: 他们发现它完全被虫子吃掉了。

sentences.en: It's rotten with worMs.
sentences.zh: 它被虫蛀烂了。

sentences.en: And so they haul it onto the beach and they burn it and have a huge bonfire and then they sail back.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把它拖到海滩上烧掉，举行了一场巨大的篝火晚会，然后启程回航。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So dubious behavior all around.
sentences.zh: 所以到处都是可疑的行为。

sentences.en: They get back to Lisbon in December 1488.
sentences.zh: 他们于1488年12月回到里斯本。

sentences.en: They've been away for 16 months.
sentences.zh: 他们已经离开16个月了。

sentences.en: They've discovered more than a thousand miles of new coastline.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了超过一千英里的新海岸线。

sentences.en: Well, discovered, I mean, the people who live there knew it was there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，说是发现，我是说，住在那里的人早就知道它在那里。

sentences.en: But the key thing is that they've discovered that you can round Africa.
sentences.zh: 但关键是他们发现可以绕过非洲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which, of course, the Phoenicians knew and Herodotus reports it.
sentences.zh: 当然，腓尼基人早就知道了，希罗多德也对此有记载。

sentences.en: So if he'd been reading his Herodotus, he would have known that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他读过希罗多德，他就会知道这一点。

sentences.en: But, you know, there are other ways of finding out.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，还有其他发现的方法。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, the best part of four years before Columbus.
sentences.zh: 当然，这比哥伦布早了整整四年多。

sentences.en: So this explains, this is one of the key reasons why the Portuguese think, well, what's the point in you heading out to the West?
sentences.zh: 所以这就解释了，这是葡萄牙人认为“你们为什么要向西航行？”的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: We've already found that we can get around Africa.
sentences.zh: 我们已经发现我们可以绕过非洲了。

sentences.en: Was this publicized or were the Portuguese keeping it to themselves?
sentences.zh: 这是公开的，还是葡萄牙人想独占这个秘密？

sentences.en: I think it's not immensely well publicized because I think there's an enormous amount of emerging rivalry, I guess, between the Portuguese on the one hand and Castile and
sentences.zh: 我觉得这并没有被大肆宣传，因为我觉得葡萄牙和卡斯蒂利亚以及阿拉贡之间出现了巨大的竞争。

sentences.en: Aragon on the other.
sentences.zh: 阿拉贡。

sentences.en: Because, of course, up to this point, there's been no Spain.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，在那之前，还没有西班牙这个国家。

sentences.en: So the Portuguese are just one of many competing Iberian kingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以葡萄牙只是众多相互竞争的伊比利亚王国之一。

sentences.en: But with the marriage of Ferdinand and Isabella, you have this sort of big self-confident and the conquest of the Alhambra and Granada.
sentences.zh: 但随着费迪南德和伊莎贝拉的联姻，以及对阿尔罕布拉宫和格拉纳达的征服，你们有了一个自信心爆棚的国家。

sentences.en: So that's 1492, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是1492年，对吧？

sentences.en: So the Portuguese are aware that there's this big rival now.
sentences.zh: 所以葡萄牙人意识到现在有一个强大的竞争对手了。

sentences.en: And there's a definite sense of competition, I think, from this point on was that wasn't really there before.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，有一种明确的竞争感，我觉得这是以前没有的。

sentences.en: And the Portuguese defining themselves against the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人开始在西班牙人的对立面定义自己。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that they would want to hold on to – sometimes they want to trumpet it, to boast, but sometimes they want to kind of keep it to themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想保住这个秘密是有道理的——有时他们想大肆宣扬、吹嘘，但有时他们想把它藏着掖着。

sentences.en: And that is the context for in 1494, so two years after Columbus crosses the Atlantic, the
sentences.zh: 这就是1494年的背景，也就是哥伦布横渡大西洋两年后，臭名昭著的《托尔德西利亚斯条约》签署，当时西班牙和葡萄牙基本上瓜分了世界。

sentences.en: notorious Treaty of Tordesillas, when basically the Spanish and the Portuguese divide the world up between them.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且葡萄牙人——我的意思是，人们并不真正知道这一点，但葡萄牙人实际上欺骗了西班牙人。

sentences.en: And the Portuguese – I mean, people don't really know this, but the Portuguese trick the
sentences.zh: 他们派出了更优秀的谈判代表去托尔德西利亚斯，基本上篡改了最初的协议。

sentences.en: Spanish effectively.
sentences.zh: 所以协议是他们要在世界上画一条垂直线，简单来说，西班牙得到西半部，葡萄牙得到东半部。

sentences.en: They send much better negotiators to Tordesillas, and they basically fiddle with the original deal.
sentences.zh: 所以葡萄牙人已经向东航行，他们将获得非洲和印度等地，而西班牙将获得西部。

sentences.en: So the deal was they're going to draw a vertical line down the world, and in very, very simplistic terms, the Spanish will get the western half, and the Portuguese get the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 但葡萄牙人基本上说服了西班牙人同意将这条线向西移动1000英里。

sentences.en: So the Portuguese have already gone east, and they're going to get Africa and the Indies and so on, and the Spanish will get the weSt.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没这么做，他们后来就没资格获得巴西了。

sentences.en: But the Portuguese, they basically persuade the Spanish to agree to shift the line by 1,000 miles to the weSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么有人争论说葡萄牙人当时已经发现了巴西的原因之一。

sentences.en: And if they hadn't done that, they wouldn't have then been entitled to get Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们当时已经发现了巴西。

sentences.en: And so this is one of the reasons why people have argued that Portugal had already discovered
sentences.zh: 但我们一直在描述葡萄牙船只如何开始向西转向并利用风力。

sentences.en: Brazil by this point.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们可能在外面看到了一些东西，这并非不可能。

sentences.en: I don't think they'd discovered Brazil by this point.
sentences.zh: 是有可能的。

sentences.en: But we've been describing how Portuguese ships are starting to veer out westwards and ride the winds.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: So I think it's not beyond the bounds of possibility that they might have seen something out there.
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: It's possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们并没有定居巴西。

sentences.en: I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 他们又过了几十年才真正殖民巴西。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, they don't settle Brazil.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的首要目标，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't really colonize Brazil for another few decades.
sentences.zh: 不，因为他们还在考虑祭司王约翰、香料……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 还有印度。

sentences.en: It's not their prime objective, is it?
sentences.zh: 《托尔德西利亚斯条约》，他们……

sentences.en: No, because they're still thinking about Prestigeon, spices…
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种瓜分世界在当时只是名义上的。

sentences.en: And India.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，他们所做的只是偶尔派出一艘船绕过去。

sentences.en: The Treaty of Tordesillas, where they've…
sentences.zh: 但他们有一位新国王，曼努埃尔。

sentences.en: I mean, this sort of carving up the world is pretty notional at this point.
sentences.zh: 曼努埃尔是航海家亨利的侄孙。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, all they've done is they've sent the odd sort of ship around.
sentences.zh: 他非常好战。

sentences.en: But they have this new king, Manuel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他确实有一种深刻的使命感，即我们要夺取香料贸易。

sentences.en: Manuel is the great nephew of Henry the Navigator.
sentences.zh: 我们要摧毁伊斯兰教。

sentences.en: And he is very militant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们已经证明我们可以绕过非洲了。

sentences.en: I mean, he really has this profound sense of mission that we will grab the spice trade.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: We will destroy Islam.
sentences.zh: 你知道，让我们大干一场。

sentences.en: You know, we've shown we can get around Africa.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，还要摧毁威尼斯。

sentences.en: Let's get it on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是……

sentences.en: You know, let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为威尼斯人显然……

sentences.en: And coincidentally, destroy Venice as well.
sentences.zh: 没错，削弱威尼斯。

sentences.en: I mean…
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，当你想到这一点时，50、60年前，葡萄牙什么都不是。

sentences.en: Yes, because the Venetians obviously…
sentences.zh: 它只是边缘地带的一条小鱼。

sentences.en: Yeah, undercut Venice.
sentences.zh: 而现在它正在瓜分世界。

sentences.en: So actually, when you think about it, 50, 60 years before, Portugalism, nothing.
sentences.zh: 现在，因为这些出色的船只，他们的野心确实是无边无际的。

sentences.en: It is a minnow on the absolute fringe.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，他求助的那个人可能是所有这些葡萄牙人物中最著名的一个。

sentences.en: And now it's dividing the world up.
sentences.zh: 那就是瓦斯科·达·伽马。

sentences.en: And now, because of these splendid ships, their ambitions really are pretty boundless.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我们应该休息一下。

sentences.en: And it's at this point that, you know, the guy that he turns to is probably the most famous of all these Portuguese characters.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们应该讲述瓦斯科·达·伽马前往印度的非凡而血腥的故事。

sentences.en: And that is Vasco da Gama.
sentences.zh: 所以休息后见。

sentences.en: So I think we should take a break.
sentences.zh: 一会儿见。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we should tell the extraordinary but bloody story of Vasco da Gama's voyage to India.
sentences.zh: 一会儿见。

sentences.en: So we'll see you after the break.
sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。

sentences.en: See you in a minute.
sentences.zh: 今天所有相关的背景都将构建成一个框架。

sentences.en: See you in a minute.
sentences.zh: 并分发成作战命令。

sentences.en: We would need to understand the policy context.
sentences.zh: 或者碎片化指令。

sentences.zh: 他派遣大使前往缅甸、泰国和苏门答腊。

sentences.zh: 他拥有绘制印度尼西亚东部地图的船队。

sentences.en: He sends ships to Canton in China.
sentences.zh: 他派遣船只前往中国的广州。

sentences.en: And you, of course, they'll grab Macau, won't they?
sentences.zh: 当然，他们后来还占领了澳门，对吧？

sentences.en: Macau, exactly, yes.
sentences.zh: 澳门，没错，是的。

sentences.en: It's not just the violence.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是暴力。

sentences.en: It's also incredible kind of pioneering voyages.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种令人难以置信的开拓性航行。

sentences.en: Amazing current, yeah.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的潮流，是的。

sentences.en: And they get to Japan, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们还到了日本，对吧？

sentences.en: Don't they found a colony in Nagasaki?
sentences.zh: 他们不是在长崎建立了一个殖民地吗？

sentences.en: They do, yeah, unbelievably.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实建立了，难以置信。

sentences.en: So a little bit later, 1543, they get to the southern bit of Japan, the first Europeans to reach there.
sentences.zh: 所以稍晚一点，1543年，他们到达了日本南部，是第一批到达那里的欧洲人。

sentences.en: And then they actually founded Nagasaki, the Jesuits, I think it was.
sentences.zh: 然后他们实际上建立了长崎，我想是耶稣会士做的。

sentences.en: Again, very little known in the kind of Anglo-Saxon world, but an astonishing sort of, just the visionary scale of the achievement.
sentences.zh: 同样，这在盎格鲁-撒克逊世界里鲜为人知，但这种成就的远见卓识令人震惊。

sentences.en: Of course, one carried out with enormous violence.
sentences.zh: 当然，这一切都是伴随着巨大的暴力进行的。

sentences.en: And since we've had so much violence, maybe we should have some, a tiny bit of, well, it's still violent, but it's a bit of light relief.
sentences.zh: 既然我们已经谈论了这么多暴力，也许我们应该来点，一点点，好吧，虽然还是有点暴力，但算是一种轻松的调剂。

sentences.en: Because Albuquerque also sends back to Lisbon a white elephant and a white rhino.
sentences.zh: 因为阿尔布克尔克还送回里斯本一头白象和一头白犀牛。

sentences.en: And the rhino is the one that Albrecht Dürer draws without having seen it.
sentences.zh: 那头犀牛就是阿尔布雷希特·丢勒在没见过实物的情况下画的那一头。

sentences.en: It's the first rhino to come to Europe since the time of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 这是自罗马时代以来第一头来到欧洲的犀牛。

sentences.en: And the Portuguese being the Portuguese, you know what they do with the, they get them to Lisbon and this huge crowd.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人毕竟是葡萄牙人，你知道他们怎么处理的，他们把它们弄到里斯本，面对一大群人。

sentences.en: And they say, great, now we'll, like a child, like a child saying who would win between a lion and a shark.
sentences.zh: 他们说，太棒了，现在我们要——就像孩子一样，像个孩子问狮子和鲨鱼打架谁会赢。

sentences.en: Basically, their instinct is to say, now let's see who would win the fight.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们的本能反应就是说，现在让我们看看谁会赢。

sentences.en: But the elephant runs away.
sentences.zh: 但大象跑掉了。

sentences.en: Well, it's very Roman behaviour.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这非常罗马式的行为。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: It's very, well, the elephant goes to Rome.
sentences.zh: 这非常——好吧，大象去了罗马。

sentences.en: It gets sent to the Pope, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 它被送给了教皇，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Manuel sends the white elephant to the Pope and there's a huge, there's some Indians, there's parrots.
sentences.zh: 所以曼努埃尔把白象送给了教皇，还有一大群人，一些印度人，还有鹦鹉。

sentences.en: It's a bit like a triumph, actually.
sentences.zh: 这其实有点像凯旋仪式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I wonder if that was in their mind.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在想他们当时是不是这么想的。

sentences.en: I imagine it must have been.
sentences.zh: 我想一定是。

sentences.en: They had this huge parade through the streets of Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们在罗马街头举行了盛大的游行。

sentences.en: Because they're very alert to Pliny, who is describing the wealth of the world and particularly the wealth of India.
sentences.zh: 因为他们非常关注普林尼，普林尼描述了世界的财富，特别是印度的财富。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a huge kind of influence on them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这对他们有巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So I'm sure that that must be lurking at the back of their minds, all this very Roman behaviour.
sentences.zh: 所以我肯定，所有这些非常罗马式的行为，一定潜藏在他们的脑海深处。

sentences.en: And the other Roman behaviour is that they build kind of great monuments.
sentences.zh: 另一种罗马式的行为是他们建造了各种伟大的纪念碑。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: I was just going to say, you know, talking about the Romans, the Pope calls the elephant
sentences.zh: 我正想说，你知道，谈到罗马人，教皇给那头大象取名为

sentences.zh: 汉诺，我相信这是指汉尼拔，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Hanno is a Carthaginian name.
sentences.zh: 所以汉诺是一个迦太基名字。

sentences.en: So it's an allusion to the Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个对迦太基人的影射。

sentences.en: But you were saying about the monuments, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才在谈论纪念碑，汤姆。

sentences.en: So by now, Lisbon is this, you know, which I suppose it wasn't exactly a backwater, but it's not one of the world's great cities before then.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，里斯本是这个——我想它之前并不完全是个穷乡僻壤，但在那之前它并不是世界大都市之一。

sentences.en: But now it definitely is.
sentences.zh: 但现在它绝对是了。

sentences.en: It's this incredibly colourful kind of entrepot of peoples and traders and ships and all kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其丰富多彩的贸易中心，汇聚了各国人民、商人、船只和各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: Of course, lots of slaves because the slave markets are absolutely booming.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有大量的奴隶，因为奴隶市场极其繁荣。

sentences.en: And you were saying about monuments.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了纪念碑。

sentences.en: So there are two very famous monuments.
sentences.zh: 所以有两座非常著名的纪念碑。

sentences.en: This is Manuel is the king, and it's what's called Manueline architecture.
sentences.zh: 曼努埃尔是当时的国王，这就是所谓的曼努埃尔式建筑。

sentences.en: And if you want to see, if anybody hasn't been to Lisbon and they want to go and they want
sentences.zh: 如果你想看，如果有人还没去过里斯本，他们想去，他们想

sentences.en: to see what kind of architecture you produce, if you are incredibly self-confident and sort of puffed up with your own glory, then you go to Belen, which is in the sort of western
sentences.zh: 看看如果你极其自信，沉浸在自己的荣耀中，会创造出什么样的建筑，那么你就去贝伦，它在里斯本的西部

sentences.en: bit of Lisbon, it's where Vasco da Gama had set off from.
sentences.zh: 那一带，那是瓦斯科·达·伽马出发的地方。

sentences.en: And it's where he's buried, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 也是他埋葬的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think in the monastery.
sentences.zh: 我想是在修道院里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there are two very, really famous buildings that are symbols of Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 所以有两座非常著名的建筑是里斯本的象征。

sentences.en: So one is what's called the Tower of Belen, which is this sort of fort, sort of watch tower kind of building, very ornate, decorated with the heads of the white rhinoceros and all
sentences.zh: 一个是所谓的贝伦塔，它是一种堡垒，一种瞭望塔式的建筑，非常华丽，装饰着白犀牛的头和所有

sentences.en: these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 这些东西。

sentences.en: So the classic kind of monument that you see is a symbol of Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的这种经典纪念碑是里斯本的象征。

sentences.en: And the other, which is even more impressive, is this monastery, the monastery of the, are they called the Hieronymites?
sentences.zh: 另一个更令人印象深刻的是这座修道院，是叫热罗尼莫斯修道院吗？

sentences.en: They call the Geronimos in, I don't know what the Hieronymites are, there must be an
sentences.zh: 他们叫它热罗尼莫斯，我不知道热罗尼莫斯是什么，那一定是一个

sentences.en: order of monks, but it's this massive monastery, again, unbelievably ornate, the sort of gorgeous
sentences.zh: 修士会，但这是一座巨大的修道院，同样华丽得令人难以置信，那种华丽的

sentences.en: stonework.
sentences.zh: 石雕。

sentences.zh: 汤姆，我知道你在这个播客里喜欢谈论吃喝，就是在那座修道院里，他们发明了蛋挞。

sentences.en: Oh, the famous Portuguese custard tart.
sentences.zh: 哦，著名的葡萄牙蛋挞。

sentences.en: So the Pastejo de Nato, or the Pastejo de Belen, which you can buy in this, there's a very famous kind of cafe next to the monastery, or just across the road from the monastery,
sentences.zh: 所以是贝伦蛋挞，你可以在这里买到，修道院旁边有一家非常著名的咖啡馆，或者就在修道院马路对面，

sentences.zh: 叫贝伦古老糕点店。

sentences.en: And there, the custard tart, and actually Roger Crowley ends his book about the age of Vasco de Gama with the custard tarts, because he says they're basically a symbol.
sentences.zh: 在那里，蛋挞——实际上罗杰·克劳利在他的关于瓦斯科·达·伽马时代的书中以蛋挞结尾，因为他说它们基本上是一个象征。

sentences.en: They are a symbol of Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 它们是葡萄牙的象征。

sentences.en: Have they got coffee, by the way?
sentences.zh: 顺便问一下，他们有咖啡吗？

sentences.en: Because you have coffee with it, which is obviously an import, but they're dusted with cinnamon.
sentences.zh: 因为你配着咖啡吃，这显然是进口的，但上面撒了肉桂粉。

sentences.en: And the cinnamon is the perfect symbol of what they've gone to India to get, the spice trade.
sentences.zh: 而肉桂正是他们去印度想要获取的东西的完美象征，即香料贸易。

sentences.en: So he says cinnamon, sugar, coffee, that combination.
sentences.zh: 所以他说肉桂、糖、咖啡，这种组合。

sentences.en: But they, I mean, they have gone to India for the spice, but they've also gone to India as part of a kind of global crusade against Islam and to find Presto John.
sentences.zh: 但他们——我是说，他们去印度是为了香料，但他们去印度也是为了对抗伊斯兰教的全球十字军东征的一部分，也是为了寻找祭司王约翰。

sentences.en: And presumably- It wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 大概——那根本不存在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: By this point, so what, 1520, say, they've realised Presto John isn't out there.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，比如说1520年，他们已经意识到祭司王约翰并不存在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so their focus now, presumably, is starting to turn just a trade.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在的重心大概开始转向纯粹的贸易了。

sentences.en: Yes, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, I think they also realise now that Islam is not going to be defeated overnight, certainly by the 1520s or 1530s.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想他们现在也意识到伊斯兰教不会在一夜之间被击败，至少在1520年代或1530年代是这样。

sentences.en: And also they're starting to, there's a point at where, I guess there's a point with all of these things, with any empire builders, where the focus sort of tips from exploring
sentences.zh: 而且他们也开始——我想对于所有这些帝国建设者来说，都有一个转折点，重心从探索

sentences.en: and the sort of the glamour to the sort of humdrum job of administering.
sentences.zh: 和那种魅力转向了行政管理的琐碎工作。

sentences.en: And the Portuguese are actually not very good at the latter.
sentences.zh: 而葡萄牙人实际上并不擅长后者。

sentences.zh: 那么，这个在16世纪过程中出现的帝国，在多大程度上是后来欧洲帝国的原型？

sentences.en: So it's based on the seas, which the Dutch and the British empires will be as well.
sentences.zh: 它是基于海洋的，荷兰和英国帝国也将如此。

sentences.en: And basically it seems to consist of establishing nodes across the world.
sentences.zh: 基本上它似乎由在全球建立节点组成。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then linking them up and using them as trade.
sentences.zh: 然后将它们连接起来并利用它们进行贸易。

sentences.en: And that's basically where the Dutch and the British will, and the English and then the
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是荷兰和英国，以及后来的

sentences.en: British will do as well.
sentences.zh: 英国也会做的事情。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我想你是完全正确的，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly what it is.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是它的本质。

sentences.zh: 所以我认为它在某些方面与西班牙帝国非常不同，西班牙帝国见证了来自西班牙的大规模移民。

sentences.en: I mean, one reason they're able to overwhelm, you know, the Aztecs or the Incas is so many people arriving.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们能够压倒阿兹特克人或印加人的一个原因是大量人口的涌入。

sentences.en: But it's also land-based, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但它也是基于陆地的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I know they have to bring all the gold back in ships, but it's not like, I suppose the Spanish are as well, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我知道他们必须用船把所有的黄金运回来，但这不像——我想西班牙人也是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're getting the Philippines and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们正在占领菲律宾等等。

sentences.en: They are, but they're also, they're expanding, as you say, by land and by sea, I guess, but also by land through the Americas.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是，但他们也在扩张，正如你所说，通过陆路和海路，我想，但也通过美洲的陆路。

sentences.en: The Portuguese are obviously not doing that in India.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人在印度显然没有这样做。

sentences.en: They're taking little coastal enclaves and using them as trading posts, but they're not
sentences.zh: 他们占领了沿海的小块飞地并将其用作贸易站，但他们并没有

sentences.en: settling, you know, abroad in huge numbers.
sentences.zh: 在国外大量定居。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously we'll come to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我是说，显然我们会谈到巴西。

sentences.en: I think we'll probably come to Brazil in our next episode because the great expansion into
sentences.zh: 我想我们可能会在下一集谈到巴西，因为对巴西的伟大扩张

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 关于荷兰人和葡萄牙人之间这种激烈的竞争。

sentences.zh: 实际上，有一次，荷兰人基本上接管了葡萄牙帝国的大部分，然后葡萄牙人又夺了回来。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think it's a really, it's the prototype for the Dutch empire, I think, and for aspects of the British empire, the Portuguese empire.
sentences.zh: 但是的，我认为这确实是荷兰帝国和英国帝国某些方面的原型，葡萄牙帝国。

sentences.en: I mean, the Portuguese are not good at running it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，葡萄牙人不擅长管理它。

sentences.zh: 所以到了16世纪中叶，他们已经——你知道，有无休止的总督在互相争斗。

sentences.en: I mean, they're literally fighting against each other.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们实际上是在互相争斗。

sentences.en: Like the kings will send out governors who have to fight their predecessors to get hold of these, these sort of forts and trading stations.
sentences.zh: 就像国王会派出总督，他们必须与前任作战才能控制这些堡垒和贸易站。

sentences.en: Brazil, they go to in the 1530s.
sentences.zh: 巴西，他们是在1530年代去的。

sentences.zh: 显然，奴隶贸易开始成为一个越来越大的问题。

sentences.en: We'll probably talk about that next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次可能会谈谈这个。

sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，到了16世纪中叶，有一种动力丧失的感觉，我想说，还有使命感的丧失。

sentences.en: The sense that basically the Portuguese are inventing, well, a crucial aspect of modernity,
sentences.zh: 那种认为葡萄牙人基本上是在发明——嗯，现代性的一个关键方面，

sentences.zh: 嗯，塞巴斯蒂昂在还是个男孩时继位，他的祖母，然后是一位红衣主教为他管理国家。

sentences.en: Well, the cardinal is his uncle, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那位红衣主教是他的叔叔，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Uh, and he's a crucial figure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是一个关键人物。

sentences.en: Um, so he, and he is known as Henrique the Chaste.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以他，他被称为贞洁的恩里克。

sentences.en: Well, that's pretty good for a cardinal, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于红衣主教来说这很不错，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, but this, this, this will become an important part of what then happens.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，但这将成为后来发生的事情的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so Sebastian becomes, or Sebastiao in Portuguese, he comes of age in, in 1568.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以塞巴斯蒂昂在1568年成年了。

sentences.en: And I guess, I wonder whether there's a sense that Portugal's great glory days are already ebbing into the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我想，人们或许会觉得葡萄牙昔日的辉煌已渐行渐远，成为过去。

sentences.en: And so that makes him even more determined to sort of stake his own.
sentences.zh: 这让他更加下定决心，要开创属于自己的一番事业。

sentences.en: To cut a dash.
sentences.zh: 要大显身手。

sentences.en: Yes, to cut a dash.
sentences.zh: 没错，要大显身手。

sentences.en: And he decides he's going to lead a crusade against the Moroccans.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定发动一场针对摩洛哥人的十字军东征。

sentences.en: And he makes a terrible error, Tom, which is to trust Philip II of Spain, who says to him.
sentences.zh: 但他犯了一个严重的错误，汤姆，那就是信任了西班牙的腓力二世，后者对他说了些话。

sentences.en: Rookie's error.
sentences.zh: 新手才会犯的错。

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实。

sentences.en: I'll, I'll send you supporters.
sentences.zh: 我会，我会派援军给你的。

sentences.en: I'll send, you know, people to help you.
sentences.zh: 我会派，你知道的，派人去帮你。

sentences.en: They all assemble, all these troops and mercenaries, they assemble at Cadiz and the Spanish are nowhere to be seen.
sentences.zh: 他们集结了，所有这些军队和雇佣兵，他们在加的斯集结，却根本不见西班牙人的踪影。

sentences.en: You know, all these promised Spanish reinforcements aren't there, but they go anyway, Sebastiao and his men.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有那些承诺的西班牙援军都没到，但塞巴斯蒂安和他的部下还是出发了。

sentences.en: So this is 1578.
sentences.zh: 那是1578年的事了。

sentences.en: They cross the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 他们横跨地中海。

sentences.en: They land in Morocco.
sentences.zh: 他们在摩洛哥登陆。

sentences.en: And I mean, you were in a previous episode, I think it was, Tom, you were, you were complimenting the crusades.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在之前的某一集里，我想是汤姆你，你当时在称赞十字军东征。

sentences.en: But this is not a crusade that goes, you said some crusades went better than others.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一场顺利的东征，你说过有些东征比其他的要成功。

sentences.en: This is one that doesn't go well.
sentences.zh: 而这一场却很不顺利。

sentences.en: Doesn't go well.
sentences.zh: 很不顺利。

sentences.en: Because in their very first battle, they're absolutely routed.
sentences.zh: 因为在他们的第一场战斗中，他们就彻底溃败了。

sentences.en: Absolutely routed.
sentences.zh: 彻底溃败。

sentences.en: And he presumably dies.
sentences.zh: 而他大概也死了。

sentences.en: He's the last scene of him as he's charging the enemy, but his body is never found.
sentences.zh: 人们最后一次见到他时，他正冲向敌阵，但他的遗体从未被找到。

sentences.en: So the mystery of what has happened to him, he leaves no heir.
sentences.zh: 所以关于他遭遇的谜团，他没有留下任何继承人。

sentences.en: And so he is succeeded by his uncle, the Cardinal, Enrique the Chaste.
sentences.zh: 于是他的叔叔，枢机主教“贞洁者”恩里克继位了。

sentences.en: But by definition, if you're called the Chaste, you're unlike, and you're kind of 60 or whatever, you're unlikely to be producing an heir.
sentences.zh: 但从定义上讲，既然被称为“贞洁者”，而且他已经60岁左右了，不太可能生下继承人。

sentences.en: And so when Enrique the Chaste dies in 1580, the guy who is next in line for the throne is none other than Philip II of Spain.
sentences.zh: 所以当“贞洁者”恩里克在1580年去世时，王位的第一顺位继承人正是西班牙的腓力二世。

sentences.en: Very much not a friend, I think it's fair to say, of the rest of his history, Philip II of Spain.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，在余下的历史中，西班牙的腓力二世绝非什么好人。

sentences.en: He hasn't appeared in this podcast before, but now that he has, I just want to absolutely state my colours to the mast and say, not my favourite person.
sentences.zh: 他之前没在播客里出现过，但既然现在出现了，我必须旗帜鲜明地表明立场：他不是我喜欢的人。

sentences.en: Not a fan.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢他。

sentences.en: Well, he's not behaving well here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在这里的表现确实不怎么样。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And he essentially, well, so he says about Portugal, I inherited it, I bought it, and I conquered it.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是这么说的：关于葡萄牙，我继承了它，我买了它，我还征服了它。

sentences.en: So in every way he takes over.
sentences.zh: 所以他从各个方面接管了葡萄牙。

sentences.en: Although having said that, I think we're doing Philip II down because he does actually behave quite well.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我觉得我们对腓力二世评价过低了，因为他的表现其实还算不错。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 我是说，并没有。

sentences.en: He treats Portugal with dignity.
sentences.zh: 他对待葡萄牙还是很有尊严的。

sentences.en: Portugal remains, you know, supposedly an independent kingdom.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙依然，你知道，名义上是一个独立的王国。

sentences.en: And I think actually, Tom, we haven't really touched on this as much as we could have done, but Spain itself is a very recent creation at this point.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，汤姆，我们之前没怎么深入探讨过这一点，但西班牙本身在当时也是一个非常新的创造。

sentences.en: And, you know, Spain is itself a patchwork of kingdoms, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，西班牙本身就是由多个王国拼凑而成的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Most obviously Castile and Aragon.
sentences.zh: 最明显的例子就是卡斯蒂利亚和阿拉贡。

sentences.en: So Philip II is adding another kingdom.
sentences.zh: 所以腓力二世只是又增加了一个王国。

sentences.en: So he wouldn't necessarily absorb it because, I mean, his predecessor, Charles V, had been ruling all kinds of different places without combining them into one.
sentences.zh: 所以他未必会吞并它，因为他的前任查理五世统治着各种不同的地方，却并没有把它们合并成一个国家。

sentences.en: So the Portuguese, who already have, I think it's fair to say by now, a sense of their own distinctiveness, which has been forged in the previous hundred years because of their
sentences.zh: 所以葡萄牙人，我想公平地说，到那时已经有了强烈的独特性意识，这种意识是在过去一百年里通过他们

sentences.en: own explorations and their own missions, they have no intention of becoming Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 自己的探索和传教活动锻造出来的，他们根本没打算成为西班牙人。

sentences.en: And it's a bit like Scotland and England, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 这有点像苏格兰和英格兰，我想。

sentences.en: You can't, it's going to be very difficult to combine them.
sentences.zh: 你无法，要把它们合并起来会非常困难。

sentences.en: The parallel is, I guess, with Catalonia, which similarly has a very strong sense of its distinctiveness, gets absorbed into what will become the kingdom of Spain and stays part of
sentences.zh: 我想这与加泰罗尼亚的情况类似，它同样有着非常强烈的独特性意识，后来被并入未来的西班牙王国，并一直作为

sentences.en: Spain.
sentences.zh: 西班牙的一部分。

sentences.en: But the difference with Portugal, and the same thing might well have happened with Portugal,
sentences.zh: 但葡萄牙的不同之处在于，同样的情况也可能发生在葡萄牙身上，

sentences.en: but I suppose the difference is that Portugal does have this, I mean, it has a vast global empire that is Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 但我认为不同之处在于，葡萄牙确实拥有一个庞大的、属于葡萄牙的全球帝国。

sentences.en: And as we enter the 17th century, so there are other powers that are arriving, Protestant powers of whom the Dutch are the cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 随着我们进入17世纪，其他势力也开始涌现，其中荷兰人是新兴的强权，处于领先地位。

sentences.en: And the Dutch start to look with envious eyes at all these Portuguese possessions.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人开始用贪婪的目光注视着所有这些葡萄牙的属地。

sentences.en: And so the question of whether the Spanish monarchy will help the Portuguese to see these, you
sentences.zh: 因此，西班牙君主制是否会帮助葡萄牙人对付这些，你

sentences.en: know, these Dutch pirates as the Portuguese sees them, help see them off, is crucial to whether Portugal will become a loyal part of this emergent kingdom.
sentences.zh: 知道，在葡萄牙人眼中是海盗的荷兰人，帮助他们击退这些敌人，对于葡萄牙是否会成为这个新兴王国忠诚的一部分至关重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because also the Portuguese feel, I think, that they've been dragged into this world war against the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 因为葡萄牙人也觉得，我想，他们被拖入了这场针对荷兰人的世界大战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because they're yoked to the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 因为他们被绑在了西班牙人的战车上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the Spanish don't care about protecting the Portuguese possessions.
sentences.zh: 而且西班牙人根本不在乎保护葡萄牙的属地。

sentences.en: And the Portuguese, you definitely get this sense, I think, by the beginning of the 17th century, that Portugal has been hard done by in being sort of united with Spain.
sentences.zh: 而且葡萄牙人，我想到了17世纪初，你肯定能感觉到，葡萄牙因为与西班牙合并而受到了不公正的待遇。

sentences.en: And I think it's at that point, isn't it, where you start to get, well, you have to get at the end of the 16th century, all of these imposters.
sentences.zh: 我想就在那时，不是吗，你开始看到，好吧，你必须在16世纪末看到，所有这些冒充者。

sentences.en: So people who basically say, you know, Sebastian, who was charging towards those lines and never seen again, he's actually still, yeah, he's, he's.
sentences.zh: 所以那些人基本上说，你知道，塞巴斯蒂安，那个冲向敌阵再也没回来的人，他其实还活着，是的，他……

sentences.en: Despite the fact I can't speak Portuguese in one of them.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上其中一个连葡萄牙语都不会说。

sentences.en: Well, there's one of them who's, so the first one is a sort of a guy who's, he's just an ordinary commoner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中有一个，第一个人是个普通平民。

sentences.en: Then there's a guy who's a stonecutter from the Azores.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个来自亚速尔群岛的石匠。

sentences.en: He's obviously not, he's, he's very poorly treated.
sentences.zh: 他显然不是，他受到了非常恶劣的对待。

sentences.en: He's hanged.
sentences.zh: 他被绞死了。

sentences.en: But isn't the one who doesn't speak Portuguese at all?
sentences.zh: 但那个连葡萄牙语都不会说的人不是他吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he's from Naples.
sentences.zh: 是的，他来自那不勒斯。

sentences.en: He doesn't.
sentences.zh: 他不会说。

sentences.en: So, yes, I think that's pretty, it's very Perkin, Warbeck and Lambert Simnel, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我觉得这很像珀金·沃贝克和兰伯特·西姆内尔的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: But basically it becomes clear that he is dead.
sentences.zh: 但基本上很明显他已经死了。

sentences.en: And so then you start to get these kind of weird King Arthur type stories that actually he, he is hidden away and he's waiting to come back.
sentences.zh: 于是你开始听到各种奇怪的亚瑟王式的故事，说他其实被藏了起来，正等待着回归。

sentences.en: And this is a fantasy that sustains the Portuguese under Spanish rule.
sentences.zh: 这是一种支撑着西班牙统治下葡萄牙人的幻想。

sentences.en: But I still think, I still think it's possible that Portugal might have accepted Spanish rule, except for what happens in the 17th century, which is basically the First World War.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然认为，如果不是因为17世纪发生的事情，也就是基本上第一次世界大战，葡萄牙可能还是会接受西班牙的统治。

sentences.en: And I think that we should take a break here, come back tomorrow with a further episode, and we will begin with the First World War.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该在这里休息一下，明天回来继续下一集，我们将从第一次世界大战开始讲起。

sentences.en: So we will see you then.
sentences.zh: 那么我们到时见。

sentences.en: See you then.
sentences.zh: 到时见。

sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 拜拜。
